version.note: The performing edition and any cuts or retouchings by the conductor are not identified in the sources consulted.

date.value: 28 and 30 April 1927: part 1 on 28 April, parts 2 and 3 on 30 April
date.note: Bolig dates CVE-29055 (part 1) to 28 April 1927 and CVE-29056 and CVE-29057 (parts 2 and 3) to 30 April 1927; the Internet Archive description and Pristine give the two session days for the symphony. Bolig calls the movement “Allegro con moto”; the usual marking is Andante con moto.

place.value: Academy of Music, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States

label.note: Stokowski’s earlier acoustic recording of 1924 used the same matrix numbers without the CVE prefix and different issue numbers (Bolig lists 74894–74897 and 6459–6460); this transfer is the electrical recording of 1927 by its description, session dates and Victor numbers.

catalogue.note: The Internet Archive description says “Originally issued as Victor 6663, 6664 & 6665. (Later as a set as M-16.)”; Pristine gives the same numbers and album. Bolig also lists later Victor and HMV issues of the same sides. The disc and side on which the movement boundary falls are not identified; the allocation of matrices to movements follows Bolig’s part numbers.

matrixTakeSides.value: Parts 1–3: CVE-29055, take 7 (Bolig) or take 6 (Pristine); CVE-29056, take 7; CVE-29057, take 7
matrixTakeSides.note: The two discographic sources agree on the matrices and on takes 7 for CVE-29056 and CVE-29057 but differ on the take of CVE-29055. Neither can be checked against a label image here, and the DAHR matrix pages could not be opened on 17 October 2026 (503 error).

credits.note: The Internet Archive description reads “Transfer by Bob Varney”.

date.note: No transfer date is identified. The Internet Archive item was added on 24 January 2011, which is an upload date.

processing.note: The stylus, equalisation, speed and noise treatment are not documented. The file runs 12:55; Pristine’s own restoration runs 12:00, so the two transfers differ by a few seconds, and where the side joins fall in this file is not known.

digital.format: MP3 derivative supplied by the Internet Archive; an Ogg Vorbis derivative is also listed

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Schubert died in 1828. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: The Internet Archive item carries a CC0 licence URL declared by the uploader, which is not treated as authority to waive Victor’s rights. The pre-1963 European rule applies because the recording was made in 1927 and issued on Victor 6663–6665 long before 1963, so the 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension; the exact issue year is not stated in the sources consulted. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence. The recording was published after 1925, so a US public-domain basis is not established.

alternatives.value: Pre-1963 European public domain — territorial basis.
CC0 — licence URL on the Internet Archive item, uploader’s declaration.
